title: Survey review UI, correction workflow, and profile integration (Packet C)
objective: Design and build the survey review experience (owner directive 2026-07-20, survey workstream Packet C). (1) REVIEW SCREEN: clean, progressively disclosed; shows the original survey document with extracted lines, boundaries, labels, and measurements overlaid; highlights uncertain or conflicting values; lets an AUTHORIZED user accept, correct, or reject each material item. (2) CORRECTIONS: every correction is auditable (who/when/what/why), causes dependent calculations to rerun, and NEVER overwrites the immutable source file or erases the original extraction (correction history per the survey-evidence contract). (3) STATES: use the explicit states uploaded / processing / auto_extracted / needs_review / rejected / professionally_confirmed. 'Verified' is NOT automatically the final status - the task must define exactly which licensed or designated professional role may provide professional confirmation (professional-confirmation state is granted only through that role; this is a G6-adjacent boundary and the role definition requires owner/qualified-human sign-off). (4) DOWNSTREAM HONESTY: show which buildability conclusions are blocked or provisional because survey evidence is unresolved (unresolved survey items propagate visibly; no silent defaults).
business_reason: Extraction without human-controlled correction and explicit professional confirmation would let machine output masquerade as boundary truth; the review workflow is what turns ingested documents into auditable evidence (owner directive 2026-07-20).

acceptance_scenarios: SC-S1 primary journey: reviewer opens a needs_review survey, sees overlay + highlighted uncertain values, accepts some, corrects one (with reason), rejects one; audit trail complete; dependent calculations rerun; states transition correctly
SC-S2 immutability: after corrections, the original file digest and original extraction records remain intact and viewable side-by-side with the corrections
SC-S3 authorization: an unauthorized role cannot accept/correct/reject or grant professional confirmation; the professional-confirmation action is available only to the defined role
SC-S4 no-auto-verified: nothing reaches professionally_confirmed without the explicit role action; auto_extracted facts display as unconfirmed evidence everywhere they appear
SC-S5 downstream honesty: a property with unresolved survey items shows exactly which buildability conclusions are blocked/provisional; resolving the item clears the flag through rerun

SC-S6 conflict display: a deterministic-check failure (e.g. area-vs-stated mismatch) is visible, plain-language explained, and unresolvable-by-click (requires correction or rejection, never dismissal)
SC-S7 recovery + a11y: recoverable API failure mid-review; keyboard navigation and accessibility pack on the new screens; responsive at supported viewports
SC-S8 regression: full repository CI green on both events; existing web e2e suites green
risks: DISPATCH HOLD: awaits owner review of the 2026-07-20 planning report AND acceptance of M2-T015 + M2-T012

STOP CONDITIONS: any path granting confirmation without the defined role; any contract change need; any production credential need
Execution: local/CI; Playwright browser evidence; low-storage compliant

SESSION 14 CORRECTION - the prior session's 'fully verified' claim was PREMATURE: CI on PR #216 had not finished when the handoff was written, and it FAILED. web-e2e (required check, run 31352797639) failed 1/277: api.test.ts SC-S4 'blocks confirmation with confirmation_rejected + rejected_fact_ids' -> AssertionError: expected ['sevdocp13'] to include 'sev:doc:p1:3'. Root cause = a REAL product defect the whole G3/G5/human-journey/DCV wave missed: decodeError sanitized detail.rejected_fact_ids with the shared boundedToken (charset [A-Za-z0-9._-]), which strips the colons out of evidence ids, so a confirmation-blocking response returned ids matching no fact.evidence_id and the UI could not point a reviewer at the blocking facts. Secondary hole in the same line: the '?? String(id)' fallback emitted the RAW unsanitized value exactly when sanitization yielded empty. FIXED at 80252d3 (branch task/M2-T016-survey-review): module-local boundedEvidenceId keeping ':' with boundedToken's defensive shape; shared boundedToken deliberately untouched (lib/api.ts + lib/rule-evaluation.ts depend on its narrow charset); unsanitizable entries dropped; parameterized adversarial sanitizer table + an end-to-end assertion added. NOT verified locally (worktree has no node_modules; local npm prohibited) - CI is the verifier. CONSEQUENCE FOR ACCEPTANCE: the 77-row DCV at d45f330 and the G3/G5/human-journey verdicts are now STALE (reviewed head moved d45f330 -> 80252d3); they need a delta re-review + re-stamp at the new head before any gate is recorded. Also recorded: M2-T016 allowed_paths are PROSE, not pathspecs ('apps/web/src/** (survey review feature areas)'), so its frozen content identity computes to the EMPTY-SET hash e3b0c442 and binds no code at all - a real weakness in the identity machinery, logged for a follow-up rather than changed now (editing allowed_paths would move the material digest and invalidate the existing verification).

SECOND DEFECT, more serious than the first. Fixing the vitest failure let Playwright run for the FIRST TIME on this branch (at d45f330 the web-e2e job died at the vitest step before Playwright started), and ALL SEVEN survey-review e2e specs failed identically - survey-review-authorization SC-S3/SC-S4, survey-review-journey SC-S1 x2, survey-review-recovery-a11y SC-S7 x3 - with getByTestId('focused-item') never appearing because /survey/review/<digest> served a 404. ROOT CAUSE: both route files (src/app/survey/review/page.tsx and .../[documentId]/page.tsx) call surveyReviewEnabled() but declare NO dynamic export, so Next evaluates INTERNAL_SURVEY_REVIEW_ENABLED during next build - where it is unset - and bakes notFound() into a static page; next start with the flag set cannot undo it. This is a PRODUCT bug, not a harness quirk: config.ts documents the flag as a non-public runtime flag 'read fresh each call', and /dashboard - the pattern these routes explicitly say they mirror - already declares export const dynamic='force-dynamic' for exactly this reason. In any deployment setting the flag at runtime the survey-review screens would have 404'd. FIXED at 749f9dd (force-dynamic on both routes; the gate itself unchanged and still fail-safe off). PROCESS FINDING for the gate wave: M2-T016's own required output is a 'UI human-journey acceptance pack: browser automation + independent manual-style walkthrough', yet the browser-automation half was never green - the human-journey reviewer returned PASS without a passing e2e run, and the producer's checkpoint was submitted before CI finished. The G3/G4 evidence standard needs a green web-e2e run attached, not a walkthrough narrative. Verified by CI only in both fixes (no node_modules in the worktree; local npm prohibited).
